## Why This Is Asked

Tests on-device NLP design, privacy guarantees, and multilingual handling with code-switching in a beginner-friendly setting. Assesses ability to blend regex-based detection with a compact NER model and plan labeling, rollout, and evaluation.

## Key Concepts

- On-device inference with WebAssembly
- PII detection: regex patterns + lightweight NER
- Multilingual and code-switching resilience
- Privacy guarantees and staged rollout
- Evaluation metrics: precision/recall for redactions

## Code Example

```javascript
function redactPII(text) {
  const email = /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b/g;
  const phone = /\b(\+?\d{1,3}[-.\s+]?)?(\(?\d{2,4}\)?[-.\s+]?\d{3,4}[-.\s+]?\d{3,4})\b/g;
  return text
    .replace(email, "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
    .replace(phone, "[REDACTED_PHONE]");
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to additional languages?
- How would you validate redaction quality without leaking data?
